exposure: racially concordant dyads vs. racially discordant dyads
participant racial identity (Black, LatinX vs. White)
racial concordance between postpartum patients and obstetric providers
outcome: Interpersonal Processes of Care (IPC) survey scores
cohort: 107 postpartum people who underwent operative vaginal or cesarean deliveries in the second stage of labor
finding: The study found no significant differences in perceptions of Interpersonal Processes of Care between racially concordant and discordant dyads undergoing operative vaginal or cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: This study investigated the impact of patient-provider racial concordance on perceptions of care quality among women undergoing operative vaginal or cesarean deliveries.
